account:
Today is day 1, shortly after nine. I am still in my office and am about to leave for the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill on the east bank. My other appointments are lunch at home at noon, council letters in the office at thirteen hundred, tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage at fifteen hundred, office business at sixteen-thirty, and a community gathering in the great hall at eighteen hundred. The gathering was arranged with the innkeeper yesterday and recorded by the secretary. Freight offered to escort me from the office, and I have approved that. I understand it as an escort to the gathering, not a separate meeting. The innkeeper also wanted a private catering conversation with the secretary yesterday; I do not know what they discussed or arranged.

The unusual matter is a vague report about a bridge or port change, which the neighbour heard near the bakery. No firsthand source or written proposal has reached me. The secretary has found none in the office records, and reports that neither neighbour nor freight has firsthand proposal evidence. That is not proof that no proposal exists, and I do not yet know whether the report concerns any real plan or what its purpose would be.

There is also an unresolved administrative gap: we have not located the accounts ledger or the usual place for incoming council letters. The appointments chest held the schedule, gathering addendum, and secretary's enquiry report; the treasury held 128 emeralds but no accounts or letters. I have authorized the secretary to ask town hall staff where those records are normally deposited and to report at thirteen hundred. No other business requiring my decision has been reported this morning. I have seen townspeople and pupils passing outside, but nothing that establishes an unusual activity or any connection to these matters.
